topics.label: Earth
facts: Earth is the planet we live on.
Earth is round like a ball.
Most of Earth is covered by water, and the rest is land.
Earth spins around once every day, which makes day and night.

questions.q: What planet do we live on?

questions.fact: Earth is round, like a giant ball.
Oceans cover about 70 out of every 100 parts of Earth's surface.
Earth spins once every day, so part of it faces the Sun while the other part is dark.

topics.label: The Moon
facts: The Moon is a big round rock that travels around Earth.
The Moon does not make its own light; it shines by sunlight bouncing off it.
The Moon looks different in the sky because we see different parts of its sunny side.
People have walked on the Moon.

choices: A big rock that travels around Earth
A planet with people on it
questions.fact: The Moon is Earth's natural satellite, a big rocky ball.

questions.q: Where does the Moon's light come from?
questions.fact: The Moon has no light of its own; it reflects light from the Sun.

questions.q: When do we see the Moon in the sky?
questions.fact: We usually see the Moon shining at night.

questions.q: Have people walked on the Moon?
questions.fact: Astronauts first walked on the Moon in 1969.

topics.label: Stars
facts: Stars are giant balls of hot, glowing gas far away in space.
The Sun is the closest star to Earth.
Stars look small because they are so far away.
At night, when the sky is dark and clear, you can see many stars.

choices: A giant ball of hot, glowing gas
questions.fact: Stars are huge balls of hot gas that glow with their own light.

questions.q: Which star is closest to Earth?
questions.fact: The Sun is our closest star, and its light takes about 8 minutes to reach us.

questions.q: Why do stars look so small?
choices: Because they are very far away
questions.fact: Stars are enormous, but they look tiny because they are trillions of kilometres away.

questions.q: When can you see stars best?
questions.fact: Stars are easiest to see on dark, clear nights away from bright lights.

topics.label: The Sky
facts: The sky looks blue in the daytime because sunlight is scattered by tiny bits of air.
At sunset the sky can turn orange and pink because the sunlight travels through more air.
The sky looks dark at night because our part of Earth has turned away from the Sun.
On a clear night you can see stars, planets, and sometimes the Moon in the sky.

questions.q: Why does the sky look blue in the daytime?
choices: Sunlight is scattered by tiny bits of air
questions.fact: Air scatters blue sunlight more than other colours, so the sky looks blue.

questions.q: Why can the sky turn orange at sunset?
questions.fact: At sunset, sunlight passes through more air, which scatters away the blue light.

questions.q: Why is the sky dark at night?
choices: Our part of Earth has turned away from the Sun
questions.fact: Night happens when Earth spins and our side faces away from the Sun.

questions.q: What can you see in a clear night sky?
choices: Stars, planets, and sometimes the Moon
questions.fact: On a clear night you can spot stars, bright planets, and often the Moon.
